_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: Xcel Energy's Texas utility agreed to report AI camera fire detections under its approved plan. Its annual report answered that line with a count of cameras.

introduction.text: [Southwestern Public Service Company operates as Xcel Energy](c56), the Tribune reports. [Its service area covers most of the Texas Panhandle](c29), about {{number:c29}} square miles by the utility's own study. [Its resiliency plan called for AI cameras in its Tier 2 and Tier 3 wildfire risk areas](c23).

The Public Utility Commission approved the utility's resiliency plan on {{date:c10}}. [The order lists the number of artificial intelligence camera fire detections among the evaluation metrics](c33) for that plan. [SPS will include the agreed evaluation metrics in its annual resiliency plan reports](c34) under the same order.

sections.heading: What the report put on that line

paragraphs.text: [SPS filed its annual resiliency plan report](c9) on {{date:c9}}. Under the detections metric [the report gives 33 cameras installed as the actual figure and 34 for 2026 as the projection](c8). The line reports a count of cameras. It gives no count of detections.

The report states its own limits. [SPS says the partial reporting year means it can't yet compare each measure's actual effectiveness with its projected effectiveness](c21). Other lines on the same page do carry counts. [For wildfire ignitions associated with overhead power lines the report gives a single actual figure of 24](c18). [It gives 26 as the actual total of wildfires reported by the National Interagency Fire Center](c20) in counties SPS serves.

The plan application describes the system in plain terms. [Each AI camera location carries two physical cameras that rotate to detect smoke](c25). [Data from the cameras is verified and forwarded by a human operator](c24). [SPS named Pano AI as its partner and said the system's fire detections are shared with SPS and first responders](c26). [SPS said it planned to install a total of 68 AI cameras in Tier 2 and Tier 3 wildfire risk areas](c23).

[SPS budgeted $0 in 2025 capital for the AI camera project because the project was scheduled to start in 2026](c12). It reports [approximately $2M of actual capital spending on it in 2025](c13) once the order was approved. For the current year [SPS anticipates $10,537,400 of AI camera capital costs against $6,423,554 in the plan, which it calls a 64.04% change](c15). It points in part to [added system capabilities and expanded camera coverage in high-risk areas](c16).

sections.heading: What the state asks of every utility

paragraphs.text: The rule behind these plans reaches far past one company. [It applies to every electric utility, municipally owned utility and electric cooperative that owns a transmission or distribution facility in Texas](c2). The staff blueprint for writing a plan treats cameras as optional. [Its Situational Awareness section is marked Suggested and lists cameras or other monitoring technology as a tool](c37). [The PUCT said utilities are not required to use the blueprint](c38). [Pano AI had asked the commission to add a minimum requirement that plans describe their use of situational awareness solutions](c39).

Few plans had arrived when lawmakers asked. [Only eight of 160 utilities operating in fire-prone areas of Texas had complied with the wildfire mitigation plan law](c43), the Tribune reports from a House State Affairs hearing.

The report doesn't say whether the cameras detected a fire. It doesn't say they detected none either. A missing count isn't a count of zero. [SPS says its 2027 annual report will carry a full year of data](c57), and under the order that report carries the same line. The Tribune reports the company's interim president told lawmakers [the company has deployed 97 wildfire detection cameras across its service territory](c41). That count covers more than Texas.

Both documents are public on the PUCT Interchange. [The order sits in Docket 57463](c31) and [the report in Project 57941](c9). Under the state rule [the deadline to intervene in a wildfire mitigation plan case is 30 calendar days from the date service of notice is complete](c5).
